_comment: Captions written from outputs/lora/interval_verification.json and from looking at outputs/lora/contact_sheets/, not from the dataset class name. Each caption states what is visible in that clip's own 49-frame window: the scene, roughly how many people are present, and where the person using the marked walkway is. Two scenes appear. Scene A is the press line that the counterfactual source clip 0_tr143 was shot in: presses along the left, the green marked walkway along the right. Scene B is a wider aisle with presses on both sides, a corrugated metal wall and a MAMUL DEPO sign at the far end, where people appear much smaller. Distance wording follows the measured median height in pixels of the person on the walkway: about 150 px is close to the camera, about 80-130 px is the middle distance, about 40-50 px is the far end of the aisle.

_dropped.4_tr16: No one uses the marked walkway in this window. The detector finds walkway contact in 30 of 49 frames, but every one of those contacts has a foot position near x=32, at the extreme left of the frame, on green-painted machine base beside the press rather than on the marked lane at x=515-640 where every other scene-A clip's contacts fall. Confirmed visually in outputs/lora/contact_sheets/foot_check.png.
_dropped.4_tr36: No person is on the marked walkway in any of the 49 frames, and people are detected in only 40 of them, at a median height of 33 px. The interval does not show the behaviour.

4_tr1: Fixed overhead security camera above a factory aisle. Industrial press machines stand along the left with an operator in dark navy overalls working at the nearest one, and a green marked pedestrian walkway bordered by yellow lines runs along the right over a grey concrete floor. A worker walks along the green marked walkway at the far end of the aisle, small in the distance, staying inside the yellow boundary lines. Unchanged lighting, no camera movement.
